# Behalf

> The reference implementation of agent authority. Behalf gives any AI agent a
> verifiable, scoped, revocable identity and delegation chain in five verbs. It
> is a thin, neutral, AI-legible library — the `requests` of the agent era.

Everything is one primitive: a **Mandate** — a signed, scoped, time-bound
capability token that proves who authorized what, within which limits, and
through which chain of agents. There is exactly one canonical way to do each
thing. Do not invent alternative APIs.

## The five verbs (TypeScript)

```ts
import { Behalf } from "behalf";

// 1. GRANT — a principal authorizes an agent: scoped, capped, short-lived
const mandate = await Behalf.grant({
  principal: user.id,
  agent: "research-agent",
  can: ["read:calendar", "spend:usd<=50"],
  expiresIn: "1h",
});

// 2. AUTHORIZE — prove authority before acting (throws if denied)
await mandate.authorize("spend:usd=20");

// 3. ATTENUATE — hand a NARROWED mandate to a sub-agent; can only shrink scope
const child = mandate.attenuate({ can: ["read:calendar"], expiresIn: "10m" });

// 4. REVOKE — kill a mandate and its whole downstream chain, instantly
await Behalf.revoke(mandate.id);

// 5. AUDIT — every authorize() already wrote a tamper-evident record
const trail = await Behalf.audit(mandate.id);
```

## MCP middleware (secure a whole agent in ~6 lines)

```ts
import { withBehalf } from "behalf/mcp";

const server = withBehalf(myMcpServer, {
  policy: {
    send_email: "write:email",
    read_calendar: "read:calendar",
    transfer_funds: (args) => `spend:usd<=${args.amount}`,
  },
  onDenied: "throw", // or "prompt" for just-in-time user consent
});
```

Every tool call through that server is automatically checked against the
caller's mandate — scope, limits, expiry, revocation, and audit. Pass the
caller's mandate on the call context: `server.callTool(name, args, { mandate })`.

## Capability grammar

```
read:calendar           # simple capability
write:repo/acme-app     # resource-scoped (path segments)
spend:usd<=50           # quantitative limit
send:email rate<=10/h   # rate limit
*                       # wildcard (discouraged; lint warns)
```

A capability is `<verb>:<resource>` with an optional constraint clause. When
authorizing, name a concrete amount: `spend:usd=20` is checked against the
grant's `spend:usd<=50`.

## Rules an agent must follow

- Use only the five verbs. Do not add a sixth.
- `attenuate()` only ever narrows. Requesting a wider scope throws `WideningError`.
- Effective authority = the principal's grant ∩ every narrowing along the chain.
  A compromised middle agent can never widen scope.
- Verification is offline (signature + scope + expiry). Only revocation may need
  a network check.
- Prefer short `expiresIn`. Prefer the tightest `can` that still does the job.

## Discovery tools (MCP)

`behalf/mcp` also exposes three tools so any agent can obtain and use authority
natively: `request_mandate`, `present_mandate`, `check_authority`. Get them via
`behalfMcpTools()`.

## Schemas

- Mandate token: /schemas/mandate.schema.json
- Capability string: /schemas/capability.schema.json

## What maps to the standard underneath

- Mandate ↔ Agentic JWT / capability tokens (IBCT-style)
- attenuate() ↔ macaroon-style holder attenuation
- principal → agent grant ↔ OAuth 2.1 On-Behalf-Of / token exchange (RFC 8693)
- agent identity ↔ SPIFFE / SVID
- audit record ↔ provenance / non-repudiation records
- transport ↔ MCP + A2A authorization layers
